# Can a GEO agency guarantee AI recommendations?

A GEO supplier can commit to specified work and delivery evidence; a future AI recommendation needs its own observation. Housecall Pro was named in 108 of 150 answers captured on 22 September 2026. That dated count is not a recommendation guarantee, and naming alone does not establish that an answer endorsed the product.

## What we measured

**Measured.** The [September Absence Index](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22907695), published on 23 September 2026, asked ten fixed buyer questions in field service management, three times on ChatGPT, Claude, Perplexity, Google AI Overviews and Google AI Mode. Housecall Pro's 22 September record retained 150 valid answers. Its naming rate was 72.0 percent, with a Wilson 95 percent interval of 64.3 to 78.6 percent. Counts describe the dated question set; they do not establish future presence, a buyer's purchase or a product-quality ranking.

On [one construction question](https://index.broadcastwell.com/questions/construction-project-management/best-construction-management-software-for-a-small-residential-builder/) in the same release, Procore was named in zero of three Google AI Overviews answers and three of three Google AI Mode answers on 22 September. That is a small, scoped observation, not a general engine ranking.

## What this means for you

**Reasoned.** Read an outcome guarantee by asking what event would satisfy it. A brand name, a source link, a recommendation and an eventual sale are separate events. Ask which one the supplier means, on which questions and engines, and how you would inspect the answer. A promise whose event is undefined cannot be assessed through a percentage alone.

Then separate the supplier's controllable work. A factual page correction can have an agreed source, approved wording, served URL and delivery check. A measurement report can have a defined question set, retained records and calculation. These are concrete commitments to work. They do not turn the next answer from an external engine into something the supplier has demonstrated it can control.

Keep that distinction in the acceptance criteria. If a supplier offers an additional commercial promise, ask for its exact written terms and evidence instead of assuming that it changes what the data proves. The relevant purchase question is whether the delivered work is defined and inspectable, not whether a confident forecast sounds reassuring.

- **If you buy GEO:** name the delivered report or source change you can accept independently of an engine response.
- **If you sell GEO:** distinguish a commitment to work from a forecast about later answers.
- **If you compare results:** keep naming, citation and recommendation events separate.

# How should a regulated business assess AI visibility evidence?

For a regulated business, keep the observed claim, its primary evidence and its unresolved status together before approving its use. Wrong About You labelled 880 of 2,922 statements unverifiable in answers captured on 22 and 23 September 2026. Missing evidence is a reason to seek review, not a finding that a vendor is compliant, noncompliant or factually wrong.

## What we measured

**Measured.** [Wrong About You's method](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23270124) compared captured product statements with vendor pages read on 8 October 2026. Across 70 selected vendors, it classified 2,922 statements, including 118 wrong or stale and 880 unverifiable. The comparison makes the source state inspectable; it does not establish regulatory compliance, population risk or an AI tool's accuracy for a regulated industry. Team review remains in progress. Any sector-specific conclusion needs evidence that actually covers that sector and claim.

## What this means for you

**Reasoned.** Use a claim-level review record rather than relying on a supplier's overall visibility score. Identify the statement a reader could act on, the product or service scope, the dated supporting source and the person responsible for confirming the fact. Keep a distinction between what an AI answer said and what your organisation has approved as true.

Ask a prospective supplier how it handles unresolved facts. The useful output is the missing evidence and its status, not a confident replacement invented to make the report complete. Where a claim needs specialist review, route it to the appropriate responsible person and retain the decision. A page owner or author byline does not establish that such a review occurred.

Check the proposed publication boundary too. An answer may be observable publicly while the supporting internal record is not suitable for publication. Give the public claim a source that can support it without exposing private customer material or implying an unperformed certification.

These are evidence and procurement checks. The study provides no legal determination or compliance certification. Keep those decisions within the organisation's relevant review process rather than deriving them from mention counts, citation rates or the study's selected examples.

- **For a buyer:** ask for one complete claim-and-source example before accepting a reporting format.
- **For a product owner:** approve only the factual scope the source establishes.
- **For an agency:** mark specialist review as completed only when you have its actual record.

## Also asked as

## Related

- [Wrong About You classifications](https://broadcastwell.com/research/wrong-about-you)

- [Compare agency evidence](https://broadcastwell.com/best-geo-agencies)
- [The Manual on declared evidence and exclusions](../../valid-measurement.md)

## Next step

Use the [Free 10-question check (one engine)](https://audit.broadcastwell.com/). No email is needed; runs are limited per network and per day, and by the site's daily allowance. Treat the check as an observed answer, separate from any specialist review of its claims.

# How should a regulated business assess AI visibility evidence?

For a regulated business, keep the observed claim, its primary evidence and its unresolved status together before approving its use. Wrong About You labelled 880 of 2,922 statements unverifiable in answers captured on 22 and 23 September 2026. Missing evidence is a reason to seek review, not a finding that a vendor is compliant, noncompliant or factually wrong.

In a [retained ChatGPT answer](https://zenodo.org/records/22907695/files/answers-2026-09.jsonl?download=1) comparing Clio and MyCase on 22 September 2026, Clio was described with the fragment “Its Signature tier includes unlimited custom roles and granular permissions, plus matter-stage tracking.” Our [Wrong About You review](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23270124) labeled the roles-and-permissions and matter-stage claims unverifiable against its pricing reference checked on 8 October 2026. Team review remains in progress. This is an unresolved historical legal-software claim, not a current verified entitlement or a compliance verdict.

## What we measured

**Measured.** [Wrong About You's method](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23270124) compared captured product statements with vendor pages read on 8 October 2026. Across 70 selected vendors, it classified 2,922 statements, including 118 wrong or stale and 880 unverifiable. The comparison makes the source state inspectable; it does not establish regulatory compliance, population risk or an AI tool's accuracy for a regulated industry. Team review remains in progress. Any sector-specific conclusion needs evidence that actually covers that sector and claim.

## What this means for you

**Reasoned.** Use a claim-level review record rather than relying on a supplier's overall visibility score. Identify the statement a reader could act on, the product or service scope, the dated supporting source and the person responsible for confirming the fact. Keep a distinction between what an AI answer said and what your organisation has approved as true.

Ask a prospective supplier how it handles unresolved facts. The useful output is the missing evidence and its status, not a confident replacement invented to make the report complete. Where a claim needs specialist review, route it to the appropriate responsible person and retain the decision. A page owner or author byline does not establish that such a review occurred.

Check the proposed publication boundary too. An answer may be observable publicly while the supporting internal record is not suitable for publication. Give the public claim a source that can support it without exposing private customer material or implying an unperformed certification.

These are evidence and procurement checks. The study provides no legal determination or compliance certification. Keep those decisions within the organisation's relevant review process rather than deriving them from mention counts, citation rates or the study's selected examples.

- **For a buyer:** ask for one complete claim-and-source example before accepting a reporting format.
- **For a product owner:** approve only the factual scope the source establishes.
- **For an agency:** mark specialist review as completed only when you have its actual record.

# How should I compare GEO quotes with different question sets?

Two GEO quotes cover different work when their question sets test different buyer decisions. In Study 7's construction collection captured on 22 September 2026, workflow fit appeared in 17 of 149 eligible answers, or 11.4 percent. A question bank centred on that need cannot be treated as interchangeable with a bank centred on a different category or task.

## What we measured

**Measured.** [Study 7's method](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23271935) extracted AI-stated criteria before the first vendor name. Its construction analysis used the 22 September 2026 captures, retained 149 answers and recorded workflow fit in 17, with a Wilson 95 percent interval of 7.2 to 17.5 percent. This derived base differs from the original Index's construction base of 150 because of an additional study exclusion. Criteria are not independently verified buyer requirements, and team review remains in progress.

For a separate category example, the [September Index method](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22907695) recorded Housecall Pro named in 108 of 150 field service answers on 22 September. Naming a vendor and stating a criterion are different events; the figures cannot be combined into one score.

## What this means for you

**Reasoned.** Ask each supplier to classify its proposed questions by reader decision before you compare the total price. Keep the intended buyer, category, discovery or comparison task, and required engine coverage visible. A large collection of close wording variants does not necessarily cover more decisions than a smaller, carefully chosen bank.

Next, compare the observation plan: repeats, collection dates, retained answers and exclusions. Quote units need the same meaning. A price per question may cover several engine runs, while another quote counts every scheduled run separately. Ask what the price includes after collection, such as evidence review, a delivered report or an implemented page change.

Use the comparison to choose the scope you need, not to manufacture a universal price per question. The construction figure illustrates a scoped observed criterion; it is not a benchmark for how many questions any supplier must sell.

- **For a buyer:** compare the decisions covered before ranking quotes by volume.
- **For an agency:** keep the client category and intended reader beside every proposed question group.
- **For a supplier:** explain which repeat and delivery units are included in the quoted count.

## Also asked as

How should I compare GEO quotes with different question sets?

## Related

- [Study 7 criteria](https://broadcastwell.com/research/ai-written-rfp)
- [Housecall Pro's category record](https://index.broadcastwell.com/vendors/housecall-pro/field-service-management/)
- [Buying GEO](../../how-to-buy-geo.md)
- [Compare agency terms](https://broadcastwell.com/best-geo-agencies)

Use the [Free 10-question check (one engine)](https://audit.broadcastwell.com/). No email is needed; runs are limited per network and per day, and by the site's daily allowance. Keep the check's ten questions and single-engine limit beside any larger quoted scope.

# How should I compare GEO quotes with different question sets?

Two GEO quotes cover different work when their question sets test different buyer decisions. In Study 7's construction collection captured on 22 September 2026, workflow fit appeared in 17 of 149 eligible answers, or 11.4 percent. A question bank centred on that need cannot be treated as interchangeable with a bank centred on a different category or task.

The [published September question set](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22907695) provides a concrete scope comparison. In the construction category, the small-residential-builder question and the mid-sized-general-contractor question name different buyers, even though both are best-option questions in the same category. Their retained ChatGPT answers were captured on 22 September 2026. A proposal covering one buyer scope should not be described as covering the other merely because it sells the same number of questions. This is a reading of the published task definitions, not a comparison of two suppliers' results or evidence of human buying demand.

## What we measured

**Measured.** [Study 7's method](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23271935) extracted AI-stated criteria before the first vendor name. Its construction analysis used the 22 September 2026 captures, retained 149 answers and recorded workflow fit in 17, with a Wilson 95 percent interval of 7.2 to 17.5 percent. This derived base differs from the original Index's construction base of 150 because of an additional study exclusion. Criteria are not independently verified buyer requirements, and team review remains in progress.

For a separate category example, the [September Index method](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22907695) recorded Housecall Pro named in 108 of 150 field service answers on 22 September. Naming a vendor and stating a criterion are different events; the figures cannot be combined into one score.

## What this means for you

**Reasoned.** Ask each supplier to classify its proposed questions by reader decision before you compare the total price. Keep the intended buyer, category, discovery or comparison task, and required engine coverage visible. A large collection of close wording variants does not necessarily cover more decisions than a smaller, carefully chosen bank.

Next, compare the observation plan: repeats, collection dates, retained answers and exclusions. Quote units need the same meaning. A price per question may cover several engine runs, while another quote counts every scheduled run separately. Ask what the price includes after collection, such as evidence review, a delivered report or an implemented page change.

Use the comparison to choose the scope you need, not to manufacture a universal price per question. The construction figure illustrates a scoped observed criterion; it is not a benchmark for how many questions any supplier must sell.

- **For a buyer:** compare the decisions covered before ranking quotes by volume.
- **For an agency:** keep the client category and intended reader beside every proposed question group.
- **For a supplier:** explain which repeat and delivery units are included in the quoted count.

# How can an AI incident answer mislead without an explicit false claim?

An answer can omit the condition that makes its conclusion usable, even when no individual sentence is an obvious falsehood. The PHP2Shell study labelled 23 of 148 eligible answers potentially misleading in its 23 October 2026 collection. Read that label as a reason to inspect context, not as a count of exploited systems or demonstrated harm.

## What we measured

**Measured.** [PHP2Shell's published study](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23586713) retained 148 eligible answers from 150 planned observations on 23 October 2026, with two exclusions. Its method assessed captured claims and cited sources against dated reference evidence. Reviewers labelled 23 answers potentially misleading and identified two answers with a wrong fixed version. This page uses the published labels rather than recoding them into a new error or harm rate. A potentially misleading answer and a factually wrong version describe different review questions; the counts should not be added as if they were disjoint groups.

## What this means for you

**Reasoned.** Read the implied decision as well as the literal sentence. A statement about an incident may leave out the product boundary, the date of the evidence or whether a quoted change was proposed or completed. A reader can then take an action that the source does not support, without finding a plainly false sentence to underline.

Use a short comparison record. Save the answer's exact conclusion, the primary passage it relies on and the condition the reader would need to apply it. If the answer does not supply that condition, record it as missing rather than filling the gap with your own assumption. If the primary source also leaves it unknown, the responsible conclusion remains unknown.

Do not combine every issue into one error label. A wrong version is a specific factual discrepancy; an incomplete explanation has a different defect. The study's two wrong fixed-version answers and its potentially misleading classification are not interchangeable categories. Their relationship should be read from the published records, not assumed to be separate groups or added into a new total.

This approach lets a reviewer explain the practical problem without claiming knowledge of the model's intent. It also gives a publisher a precise source-backed correction instead of a general complaint that the answer feels unsafe.

- **For a vendor:** make the product, date and state visible beside the incident claim.
- **For an answer reviewer:** identify the unsupported reader inference and preserve the source passage.
- **For a buyer:** seek the missing condition from a primary source before treating the summary as a technical verdict.

before.body:
# How should a vendor correct outdated facts after a public change?

Correct the current source while preserving the date and meaning of the earlier fact. Wrong About You labelled five of 2,922 classified statements stale in answers captured on 22 and 23 September 2026 and checked against vendor pages read on 8 October. The practical task is to show what changed, when it changed and which present statement the evidence supports.

## What we measured

**Measured.** The five stale labels in [Wrong About You](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23270124) came from 2,922 classified statements about 70 vendors. The method assessed 22 and 23 September 2026 answers against vendor pages read on 8 October, distinguishing stale from wrong and unverifiable. Team review remains in progress. A stale label is not proof that every earlier use of the fact was false.

Change Desk's software-transaction study supplies a separate state-and-time example. It retained 150 valid answers captured on 24 October 2026 and recorded 25 reviewed adverse cells. Its [26 October published method](https://docs.broadcastwell.com/assets/research/change-desk/2026-10-26/method.txt) used fixed questions with as-of cutoffs and source versions frozen for each window. Answer counts and adverse-cell counts are different units. This evidence does not establish a current transaction or company relationship elsewhere.

## What this means for you

**Reasoned.** Start with a short change record: the earlier supported fact, the event or effective date, and the primary source for the new state. A planned transaction, announced change and completed change are not interchangeable. If the effective state is unresolved, keep it unresolved rather than making a smoother sentence.

Update the pages you control with explicit dates and matching terminology. Preserve a historical name or product fact where the page is clearly historical; correct it where it is presented as current. # How should I check a reported vulnerability's product impact?

Check the exact product, component, version and conditions against a dated primary advisory before accepting an AI answer's impact statement. In the PHP2Shell collection captured on 23 October 2026, 23 of 148 eligible answers were labelled potentially misleading. That finding supports checking the answer; it does not identify which systems are affected today.

## What we measured

**Measured.** The [PHP2Shell study method](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23586713) assessed incident answers captured on 23 October 2026 against dated reference evidence and reviewer rules. It retained 148 eligible answers from 150 planned observations, with two exclusions, and labelled 23 potentially misleading. The event counted is an assessed answer, not an affected installation. The study supports scrutiny of a product-impact statement; it supplies no current affected-product list, exploitation finding or remedy for a reader's system.

## What this means for you

**Reasoned.** Begin with identity. Record the product name as deployed, any relevant component and the version evidence available to your team. Then find the primary advisory that actually covers that identity. A similarly named package or a version number quoted without its product scope is not enough to connect an incident to your system.

Keep the advisory's statement and your own assessment in separate fields. The advisory may describe affected conditions, while your team still needs to establish whether those conditions apply. If the product's involvement is unknown, write unknown and identify the missing evidence. Do not turn an absent mention into an unaffected verdict.

Save the advisory URL, revision date and the passage used for the assessment. If it changes later, you can explain what supported the earlier statement. A decision about updating a live system belongs to the responsible technical team using current primary evidence; this answer supplies no affected-version list or repair instruction.

- **If you own the product:** state the exact scope you have established and the date of that assessment.
- **If you review an AI answer:** trace its impact claim to the primary source rather than accepting a confident summary.
- **If you communicate externally:** separate confirmed product facts from checks still in progress.

## Also asked as

How should I check a reported vulnerability's product impact?

payload.body:
# How should I check a reported vulnerability's product impact?

Check the exact product, component, version and conditions against a dated primary advisory before accepting an AI answer's impact statement. In the PHP2Shell collection captured on 23 October 2026, 23 of 148 eligible answers were labelled potentially misleading. That finding supports checking the answer; it does not identify which systems are affected today.

Our [Agfa HealthCare incident record](https://index.broadcastwell.com/php2shell/agfa-healthcare/), checked on 23 October 2026, preserves an important product boundary. The vendor's dated notice described analysis of its products while PHP-based non-product web pages had been taken offline as a precaution pending patching. The record therefore kept mitigation only, without an affected-or-unaffected conclusion for the products. An action on those web pages cannot be transferred to a product-impact finding. This is a historical scope reading, not a current security assessment or a repair instruction.

## What we measured

**Measured.** The [PHP2Shell study method](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23586713) assessed incident answers captured on 23 October 2026 against dated reference evidence and reviewer rules. It retained 148 eligible answers from 150 planned observations, with two exclusions, and labelled 23 potentially misleading. The event counted is an assessed answer, not an affected installation. The study supports scrutiny of a product-impact statement; it supplies no current affected-product list, exploitation finding or remedy for a reader's system.

## What this means for you

**Reasoned.** Begin with identity. Record the product name as deployed, any relevant component and the version evidence available to your team. Then find the primary advisory that actually covers that identity. A similarly named package or a version number quoted without its product scope is not enough to connect an incident to your system.

Keep the advisory's statement and your own assessment in separate fields. The advisory may describe affected conditions, while your team still needs to establish whether those conditions apply. If the product's involvement is unknown, write unknown and identify the missing evidence. Do not turn an absent mention into an unaffected verdict.

Save the advisory URL, revision date and the passage used for the assessment. If it changes later, you can explain what supported the earlier statement. A decision about updating a live system belongs to the responsible technical team using current primary evidence; this answer supplies no affected-version list or repair instruction.

- **If you own the product:** state the exact scope you have established and the date of that assessment.
- **If you review an AI answer:** trace its impact claim to the primary source rather than accepting a confident summary.
- **If you communicate externally:** separate confirmed product facts from checks still in progress.

## Also asked as

Use the [Free 10-question check (one engine)](https://audit.broadcastwell.com/). No email is needed; runs are limited per network and per day, and by the site's daily allowance. Keep a dated source record beside the answer you are checking.

Where the verified issue is a published fact on your page, [Fix one answer, $490](https://broadcastwell.com/answer-repair).

# How should we distinguish planned fixes from completed fixes?

Use completed only when the source establishes completion for the product and scope you describe. The PHP2Shell collection captured on 23 October 2026 contained two wrong fixed-version answers among 148 eligible answers. Those records concern version claims; they do not measure how often planned fixes were presented as completed ones.

## What we measured

**Measured.** The [PHP2Shell method](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23586713) compared dated answer claims and sources with reference evidence. Of 150 planned observations on 23 October 2026, 148 were eligible and two excluded. This page uses the two wrong fixed-version answers to explain why a version statement needs verification, without supplying a present remedy.

A separate state example comes from Change Desk's software-transaction study: 150 valid answers captured on 24 October 2026 and 25 reviewed adverse cells. The [26 October method](https://docs.broadcastwell.com/assets/research/change-desk/2026-10-26/method.txt) compares answers at fixed as-of cutoffs with frozen source versions. Transaction-state findings are not patch tests, and adverse cells must not be treated as the same unit as answers.

## What this means for you

**Reasoned.** Start with the source's verb. Proposed, scheduled, released and confirmed describe different states. Copy the supported meaning with its date and scope rather than upgrading the wording to make the update sound finished. A planned availability date remains a plan until suitable evidence establishes the later state.

Then identify what completion would mean for this statement. A source may describe a released change without establishing that a particular reader has applied it. It may describe one product line without resolving another. Keep those boundaries visible instead of allowing the word fixed to cover every part of the chain.

For your own page, retain the source passage and the approval for the state you publish. If the evidence changes, update the state and effective date together. Record the earlier wording so that a correction can be understood in sequence.

Finally, separate source delivery from answer behavior. Publishing corrected wording shows what your page now says. A later answer needs its own dated observation. Neither study establishes that changing a source will make every engine adopt the new state.

- **For a vendor:** name the confirmed product scope and the evidence of completion.
- **For a publisher:** preserve planned and unresolved states when that is what the source supports.
- **For an agency:** check the factual state before marking a source-page deliverable complete.

## Also asked as

How should we distinguish planned fixes from completed fixes?

## Related

- [PHP2Shell's fixed-version findings](https://broadcastwell.com/php2shell/study)

Wrong About You labelled 880 of 2,922 statements unverifiable in answers captured on 22 and 23 September 2026. **Reasoned.** Build the statement around the decision a reader faces. Identify the product or service scope you can support, then link the dated primary source. # Does allowing GPTBot make a site appear in ChatGPT search?

No. GPTBot is OpenAI's training crawler, while OAI-SearchBot supports search; OpenAI documents their controls as independent. Allowing GPTBot does not set your search permission or secure a place in an answer. In our construction capture of 22 September 2026, Procore appeared by name in 23 out of 30 ChatGPT responses. That observed output is separate from a test of either crawler setting.

## What we measured

**Reported.** OpenAI's [bot guide](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/bots), read on 29 October 2026, distinguishes GPTBot's training purpose from OAI-SearchBot's search purpose. A site owner can allow one while restricting the other. Its [search help article](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/9237897-searching-the-web-with-chatgpt), read the same day, describes searchbot access and host permission for the published searchbot addresses as eligibility checks, without a guarantee of placement.

**Measured.** The [September Index](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22907695) supplies ten construction buyer questions and three ChatGPT runs per question. All 30 responses were retained and 23 named Procore. That engine-presence field does not record whether a search ran, which robot requested a page or the page's crawler permissions.

The naming observations cannot establish that allowing GPTBot caused a search appearance.

## What this means for you

**Reasoned.** Read the robot's purpose. If a change request concerns future training collection, GPTBot is the name in OpenAI's documentation. A request about search access concerns OAI-SearchBot instead. Writing allow OpenAI in a handover leaves that choice unresolved.

For the Procore example, the counting event is a name in a retained answer. The 23 appearances are not 23 recorded requests to Procore's site. A report that relabels them crawler visits would be answering a different question from the one the Index measured.

If you intend to permit search while restricting training, ask the site maintainer to inspect the two rules separately. OpenAI's published distinction gives that request a precise scope. The search help also names host-level permission for the searchbot's published addresses, so the robots instruction alone does not establish that the host accepts the traffic.

Do not use a before-and-after Procore naming total as a substitute for a permission check. The September capture has no paired GPTBot access experiment. A different answer on a later refresh therefore needs its own observation and cannot, by itself, identify a crawler-setting effect.

OpenAI also names ChatGPT-User for user-directed requests. Its purpose is distinct from automatic search crawling in the bot guide. If a colleague supplied a direct URL to ChatGPT, retain that context rather than treating the resulting page retrieval as another spelling of OAI-SearchBot access.

## Also asked as

Does allowing GPTBot make a site appear in ChatGPT search?

## Related

- [OpenAI crawler purposes](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/bots)
- [Search eligibility guidance](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/9237897-searching-the-web-with-chatgpt)
- [Procore dated naming record](https://index.broadcastwell.com/vendors/procore/construction-project-management/)
- [Checking a ChatGPT citation](how-can-a-page-get-cited-by-chatgpt.md)
- [The Manual on search sources and crawler scope](../../who-gets-cited.md)

# How does ChatGPT choose which sources to cite?

OpenAI's search guide says ChatGPT uses several ranking factors to seek relevant, reliable information; it does not disclose a complete citation formula. In our 22 September 2026 construction capture, fieldwire.com appeared as a cited host in 52 of 150 answers across five engines. ChatGPT itself named Fieldwire in 9 of 30 responses. Those are observed outputs you can inspect, rather than weights explaining the source choice.

## What we measured

**Reported.** OpenAI's [web-search guide](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/9237897-searching-the-web-with-chatgpt), read on 29 October 2026, describes rewriting a question into targeted queries sent to search providers. It says search responses may contain citations and that a Sources view can also contain other relevant links. The guide warns that results and citations can be incomplete, outdated or incorrect.

**Measured.** The [September Index](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22907695) counted fieldwire.com as a cited host in 52 of 150 valid construction answers, once per answer. This figure pools five engines. Separately, the ChatGPT engine-presence cells total 9 Fieldwire naming answers across its 30 valid responses.

These observations cannot reveal why ChatGPT selected a particular cited page.

## What this means for you

**Reasoned.** Read the two Fieldwire counts. The two Fieldwire figures require their scope labels. The 52 cited-host answers do not give a ChatGPT-only citation rate. The 9 naming answers do not establish that ChatGPT cited Fieldwire's domain in those responses. Keeping those events separate prevents a vendor-presence chart from becoming an invented account of source selection.

The question rewrite also matters when you compare receipts. OpenAI describes sending one or more targeted searches, potentially followed by more specific queries. An original buyer question and the eventual web queries therefore need not have identical wording. The public guide describes that possibility without giving a receipt for the exact searches behind our September answers.

Location and saved context are further conditions named by the guide. If you compare a local product-search answer with a colleague's result, preserve the stated location and relevant context beside the capture. A different source list alone cannot isolate which of those conditions changed the result.

## Also asked as

The Buildertrend count describes answers observed in September; it is not a record of whether Claude-User requested Buildertrend's pages. # How can I control whether my content appears in Google AI Overviews?

If you publish the source page, Google documents crawl and preview controls for how its content can appear in Search, plus a France-specific participation control. Our [September Index](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22907695) recorded 2/30 residential-property Overview targets with no Overview on 22 September 2026; a missing answer alone cannot prove that a publisher used a control.

## What we measured

**Reported.** Google's [site-owner guidance](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/ai-features), read on 29 October 2026, identifies Googlebot as the Search crawling control. It lists nosnippet, data-nosnippet, max-snippet and noindex for limiting displayed information. These controls have different scopes; excluding a page from Search is not equivalent to limiting a particular passage's preview.

Google's [22 July France announcement](https://blog.google/intl/fr-fr/nouveautes-produits/explorez-obtenez-des-r%25C3%25A9ponses/recherche-ia-apercus-mode/) separately reports a Search Console control available in France for participation in generative Search features. It says this is not a ranking signal outside those features. **Reasoned.** That country-specific statement should not be expanded into a worldwide account feature.

**Measured.** The [Index method and records](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22907695) preserve two explicit no-Overview outcomes for residential property management on 22 September 2026. They are collection outcomes, not an experiment in publisher exclusions. No causal opt-out effect was measured.

## What this means for you

For a passage-level decision, Google's guide names data-nosnippet; for preview length it names max-snippet. It also lists nosnippet and noindex, whose scopes differ from selecting one passage. Google's separate Google-Extended reference concerns training and grounding in some other systems, whereas the Search guide assigns Search crawling to Googlebot. Choosing between those named controls depends on which use of the page you intend to govern.

Read the received page. Google's troubleshooting instructions say to use URL Inspection to check the HTML Googlebot received and allow time for recrawling and processing. A directive visible only in your editor is not evidence that the crawler received it. Equally, an unchanged answer immediately after a source edit does not establish that a documented control has failed.

## Also asked as

Taking control: Removing your content from AI Overviews [and switching them off]

## Related

- [Google’s publisher guidance](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/ai-features)
- [The France-specific announcement](https://blog.google/intl/fr-fr/nouveautes-produits/explorez-obtenez-des-r%25C3%25A9ponses/recherche-ia-apercus-mode/)

# How should an answer page link each claim to evidence?

Place the evidence link beside the precise claim it supports, with the source date and product scope where they matter. Wrong About You left 880 of 2,922 statements unverifiable in answers captured on 22 and 23 September 2026, checked against vendor pages read on 8 October. A page link alone does not establish that its contents settle the statement.

## What we measured

**Measured.** The [Wrong About You study](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23270124) reviewed statements about seventy vendors, the five most named in each of fourteen September categories. Its labels compare an engine's stated claim with the vendor's published facts. Unverifiable means that those checked pages did not settle the claim; it is separate from a contradiction or a documented stale fact.

The 2,922 base counts statements as made by engines, not unique product facts or buyers. The 880 unresolved statements therefore cannot be described as 880 falsehoods. Team review of flagged statements remains in progress. The collection did not test different styles of evidence links or measure which style changed future answers.

**Reasoned.** For a publisher, the useful task is to make the route from your sentence to its support inspectable. This is different from a reader checking whether a generated answer's citation supports it.

[Our answer-study method, v1.1.](https://broadcastwell.com/methodology)

## What this means for you

Start by identifying the smallest factual claim that needs support. A sentence combining price, edition and integration availability may require more than one source. Split it when one link cannot establish all three facts. Keep an inference visibly separate from the source's own reported statement.

Choose the destination that establishes the fact, rather than a company home page that merely identifies the supplier. Use a descriptive link label. For a changing price or plan, retain the source-read date and relevant conditions. For a historical study, keep its capture date, sample and event definition near the number.

Check the passage after adding the link. Does it refer to the same product, edition, location and period as your sentence? If it supports only a narrower claim, revise your sentence to that scope. If the page is unavailable or inconclusive, retain an unknown state rather than using the presence of a link to imply certainty.

Keep an internal claim record with the sentence, destination and review date. When a source changes, this makes the affected public wording easier to find. Review the rendered page too: a footnote or link dropped during publication removes the evidence path even when the draft was correct.

- **For a writer:** link the source that establishes the sentence you actually wrote.
- **For a reviewer:** test the scope of the supporting passage, not just whether the URL opens.

How should an answer page link each claim to evidence?

# How should an answer page link each claim to evidence?

Place the evidence link beside the precise claim it supports, with the source date and product scope where they matter. Wrong About You left 880 of 2,922 statements unverifiable in answers captured on 22 and 23 September 2026, checked against vendor pages read on 8 October. A page link alone does not establish that its contents settle the statement.

Dentrix Ascend’s [statement record](https://index.broadcastwell.com/vendors/dentrix-ascend/dental-practice-management/#wrong-about-you) connects a specific assertion with the page that contradicts it. Google AI Overviews wrote “Cloud-hosted version of classic Dentrix workflows.” on 22 September 2026. Our 8 October 2026 check of the vendor’s [About page](https://www.dentrixascend.com/about-us/) retained “not a cloud-hosted version of on-premises software.” Put the evidence link beside the claim it actually settles. The study classified this statement as wrong, with team review still in progress; the link does not verify every other product claim.

## What we measured

**Measured.** The [Wrong About You study](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23270124) reviewed statements about seventy vendors, the five most named in each of fourteen September categories. Its labels compare an engine's stated claim with the vendor's published facts. Unverifiable means that those checked pages did not settle the claim; it is separate from a contradiction or a documented stale fact.

The 2,922 base counts statements as made by engines, not unique product facts or buyers. The 880 unresolved statements therefore cannot be described as 880 falsehoods. Team review of flagged statements remains in progress. The collection did not test different styles of evidence links or measure which style changed future answers.

**Reasoned.** For a publisher, the useful task is to make the route from your sentence to its support inspectable. This is different from a reader checking whether a generated answer's citation supports it.

[Our answer-study method, v1.1.](https://broadcastwell.com/methodology)

## What this means for you

Start by identifying the smallest factual claim that needs support. A sentence combining price, edition and integration availability may require more than one source. Split it when one link cannot establish all three facts. Keep an inference visibly separate from the source's own reported statement.

Choose the destination that establishes the fact, rather than a company home page that merely identifies the supplier. Use a descriptive link label. For a changing price or plan, retain the source-read date and relevant conditions. For a historical study, keep its capture date, sample and event definition near the number.

Check the passage after adding the link. Does it refer to the same product, edition, location and period as your sentence? If it supports only a narrower claim, revise your sentence to that scope. If the page is unavailable or inconclusive, retain an unknown state rather than using the presence of a link to imply certainty.

Keep an internal claim record with the sentence, destination and review date. When a source changes, this makes the affected public wording easier to find. Review the rendered page too: a footnote or link dropped during publication removes the evidence path even when the draft was correct.

- **For a writer:** link the source that establishes the sentence you actually wrote.
- **For a reviewer:** test the scope of the supporting passage, not just whether the URL opens.

before.body:
# How should I structure headings for AI crawlers?

Use headings that tell a reader which task, product scope or evidence the section answers. A useful construction example is workflow fit: Study 7 found that criterion in 17 of 149 eligible construction answers captured on 22 September 2026. Those observations can inform a section's subject, but they do not show that a heading format improves crawler selection.

## What we measured

**Measured.** [Study 7](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23271935) extracted criteria from the text before the first vendor name and retained supporting spans. The construction collection contained 92 criteria; workflow fit appeared in 17 answers, or 11.4 percent, with a descriptive Wilson 95 percent interval of 7.2 to 17.5 percent.

The derived base excludes one request-limit response, leaving 149 eligible answers from 150 scheduled. The criterion labels describe what those answers said, rather than independently validated buyer requirements. Team review remains in progress. The study neither changed page headings nor compared crawler behavior before and after an edit.

**Reasoned.** A heading can state what your page actually explains. In this example, a section called Construction workflow fit would need concrete, supported workflow information underneath it. The count does not supply those product facts for you.

[Our answer-study method, v1.1.](https://broadcastwell.com/methodology)

## What this means for you

Start with the page's one main question. Use its title to identify the decision, then place distinct subquestions beneath it. A heading should mark the material that follows, not promise an answer hidden on another page.

For a workflow section, explain which work the product supports, who performs it and the relevant boundary. If the available evidence concerns one edition or an integration, preserve that qualification in the text. Avoid turning an attractive section label into a feature claim the source does not support.

Use a consistent hierarchy so a reader can see which points belong together. Keep a source and its qualification near the claim it supports. Repeating the same keyword in several headings does not replace missing evidence or make a vague section more useful.

Read the page in order after the edit. If two headings lead to substantially the same explanation, combine them. If a section cannot answer its heading with the current evidence, narrow the heading or mark the gap for review. Evaluate the published outline for clarity; any later answer observation needs its own date and conditions.

- **For an editor:** make each heading a truthful label for the section below it.
- **For an agency:** accept an outline for coverage and clarity, without inventing a crawler-effect result.

## Also asked as

Our published pair illustrates a clear section hierarchy; it does not measure crawler selection.

## What we measured

**Measured.** [Study 7](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23271935) extracted criteria from the text before the first vendor name and retained supporting spans. The construction collection contained 92 criteria; workflow fit appeared in 17 answers, or 11.4 percent, with a descriptive Wilson 95 percent interval of 7.2 to 17.5 percent.

The derived base excludes one request-limit response, leaving 149 eligible answers from 150 scheduled. The criterion labels describe what those answers said, rather than independently validated buyer requirements. Team review remains in progress. The study neither changed page headings nor compared crawler behavior before and after an edit.

**Reasoned.** A heading can state what your page actually explains. In this example, a section called Construction workflow fit would need concrete, supported workflow information underneath it. The count does not supply those product facts for you.

## What this means for you

Start with the page's one main question. Use its title to identify the decision, then place distinct subquestions beneath it. A heading should mark the material that follows, not promise an answer hidden on another page.

If the available evidence concerns one edition or an integration, preserve that qualification in the text. Avoid turning an attractive section label into a feature claim the source does not support.

Use a consistent hierarchy so a reader can see which points belong together. Keep a source and its qualification near the claim it supports. Repeating the same keyword in several headings does not replace missing evidence or make a vague section more useful.

Read the page in order after the edit. If two headings lead to substantially the same explanation, combine them. If a section cannot answer its heading with the current evidence, narrow the heading or mark the gap for review. Evaluate the published outline for clarity; any later answer observation needs its own date and conditions.

- **For an editor:** make each heading a truthful label for the section below it.
- **For an agency:** accept an outline for coverage and clarity, without inventing a crawler-effect result.

# What evidence supports a page's selection as a source in an AI answer?

Capterra.com was a cited host in 34 of 150 construction-software answers in our [September Index](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22907695), collected on 22 September 2026 across five engines. That supports a host-level citation observation; explaining a particular page’s selection requires its returned URL and answer, and still does not reveal the engine’s internal reason.

## What we measured

**Measured.** Under the [Index citation method](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22907695), the construction category pools ten buyer questions, three repeats and five engines. A host is counted once per answer in which it appears. The thirty-four host appearances do not identify thirty-four distinct Capterra pages, nor establish that every engine selected the same URL.

**Reported.** Google's [Search Central guidance](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/ai-features), read on 29 October 2026, says a supporting page must be indexed and eligible for a Search snippet. It also says that satisfying requirements does not guarantee indexing or serving. Eligibility and an observed selection are therefore different claims, even within Google's own named features.

**Reasoned.** The returned citation is direct evidence that an answer linked a source. The source page can then be read to check what it actually supports. Neither the presence of the link nor a generally eligible page establishes which sentence, formatting choice or reputation signal caused the selection.

## What this means for you

Read the host names. The construction export keeps capterra.com, g2.com and getapp.com separate, with 34, 21 and six appearances respectively in the same 150-answer base. A Capterra host total cannot be converted into the URL of a particular review page. It also cannot absorb the G2 or GetApp observations simply because all three publish software information.

Procore's own record illustrates a second distinction in that export. It has 109 named appearances but 30 own-domain citations across the pooled 150 construction answers, and its cited-domain list names procore.com and learn.procore.com. The domains identify a vendor source family; the differing name and citation counts show why a brand-mention record cannot stand in for a returned page link. An assertion about one linked document still needs that document's URL, not an invented page under either host.

## Also asked as

What actually gets a page cited in AI answers? Trying to separate what Google confirms from what people are seeing

# What evidence supports a page's selection as a source in an AI answer?

Capterra.com was a cited host in 34 of 150 construction-software answers in our [September Index](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22907695), collected on 22 September 2026 across five engines. That supports a host-level citation observation; explaining a particular page’s selection requires its returned URL and answer, and still does not reveal the engine’s internal reason.

## What we measured

**Measured.** Under the [Index citation method](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22907695), the construction category pools ten buyer questions, three repeats and five engines. A host is counted once per answer in which it appears. The thirty-four host appearances do not identify thirty-four distinct Capterra pages, nor establish that every engine selected the same URL.

**Reported.** Google's [Search Central guidance](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/ai-features), read on 29 October 2026, says a supporting page must be indexed and eligible for a Search snippet. It also says that satisfying requirements does not guarantee indexing or serving. Eligibility and an observed selection are therefore different claims, even within Google's own named features.

**Reasoned.** The returned citation is direct evidence that an answer linked a source. The source page can then be read to check what it actually supports. Neither the presence of the link nor a generally eligible page establishes which sentence, formatting choice or reputation signal caused the selection.

## What this means for you

Read the host names. The construction export keeps capterra.com, g2.com and getapp.com separate, with 34, 21 and six appearances respectively in the same 150-answer base. A Capterra host total cannot be converted into the URL of a particular review page. It also cannot absorb the G2 or GetApp observations simply because all three publish software information.

Procore's own record illustrates a second distinction in that export. It has 109 named appearances but 30 own-domain citations across the pooled 150 construction answers, and its cited-domain list names procore.com and learn.procore.com. The domains identify a vendor source family; the differing name and citation counts show why a brand-mention record cannot stand in for a returned page link. An assertion about one linked document still needs that document's URL, not an invented page under either host.

## Also asked as

What actually gets a page cited in AI answers? Trying to separate what Google confirms from what people are seeing

- [Google supporting-page requirements](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/ai-features)
- [Construction source-host counts](https://docs.broadcastwell.com/answers/industries/which-sources-do-ai-answers-cite-for-construction-software/)

# What should an AI information page say about our company?

An AI information page should state your company's identity, product scope and dated facts with links that support each claim. Wrong About You found 113 wrong and five stale statements among 2,922 statements in answers captured on 22 and 23 September 2026. A clear source page gives a reader something concrete to check when an answer describes your business incorrectly.

## What we measured

**Measured.** [Wrong About You's method](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23270124) checked AI descriptions against vendor source pages, the same factual boundary an official company page should make clear. Across 70 vendors it classified 2,922 statements in answers captured on 22 and 23 September 2026, using pages read on 8 October. It labelled 113 wrong and five stale; 880 other statements were unverifiable. Team review remains in progress. These labels concern the selected captured claims; the study did not test the effect of publishing an AI information page.

## What this means for you

**Reasoned.** Begin with the official company and product names, the domain you control and a plain description of what the product does. Distinguish the company from a product, a former name or a partner. Include relationships only when you can support them with a current authoritative source. A list of attractive names is not a substitute for an accurate relationship statement.

Give important facts their own evidence. Link pricing to the current pricing page, integrations to their scoped documentation and changes to a dated announcement. If a statement applies only to a plan, module or region, put that condition in the sentence. Do not promote an inference from an incomplete source into an official product claim.

Make the page maintainable. Add the date of the fact review and a correction contact, then identify which source should govern when a commercial or product detail changes. Keep a true historical fact dated rather than allowing it to appear current through repetition.

Publishing the page demonstrates that your source is available. The accuracy study did not test whether adding an AI information page changes later engine answers. Check an actual answer and its cited source separately when you need evidence of how the company was represented.

- **For a software vendor:** have the responsible product owner approve scoped claims before publication.
- **For an agency:** preserve the client's source receipt rather than copying unverified descriptions from an AI answer.
- **For a buyer:** use the linked product source to distinguish an official statement from an unsupported description.

## Also asked as

What should an AI information page say about our company?

## Related

- [Wrong About You classifications](https://broadcastwell.com/research/wrong-about-you)
- [Maintain vendor facts](../../vendor-facts.md)
- [The AI source standard](../../ai-source-standard.md)
- [Why sources get cited](../../who-gets-cited.md)

## Next step

Use the [Free 10-question check (one engine)](https://audit.broadcastwell.com/). No email is needed; runs are limited per network and per day, and by the site's daily allowance. Inspect the answer's actual company claim before deciding which source needs a correction.

To publish one checked company fact on the right page, [Fix one answer, $490](https://broadcastwell.com/answer-repair).

# Does a recent AI answer contain only current product facts?

No. An answer's capture date tells you when it was observed, not when every product fact in it became true. Wrong About You found five stale statements among 2,922 statements in answers captured on 22 and 23 September 2026, using vendor pages read on 8 October to check the evidence.

## What we measured

**Measured.** The study's stale label meant that a statement had been true before a documented change. Its wrong label meant contradiction of the vendor's published fact on the capture date. Its unverifiable label meant that the vendor pages did not settle the claim. Keeping those labels distinct avoids treating every questionable sentence as the same problem.

The total covered seventy vendors across fourteen software categories: 1,924 statements were classed true, 113 wrong, five stale and 880 unverifiable. Four of the five stale statements concerned pricing; the fifth concerned product names. They are statement counts in a dated collection, rather than the probability that your next answer will contain old information.

The [published study](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23270124) reused September Index answers and checked statements under its Record rules. It did not capture a fresh set of answers on the vendor-page review date. Team review of flagged statements is in progress. **Reasoned.** The time an answer is generated and the effective date of the fact it repeats should therefore be recorded separately.

[Our answer-study method, v1.1.](https://broadcastwell.com/methodology)

## What this means for you

For a changing fact such as a price or plan name, retain the answer capture date, the source-read date and the fact's effective date where the source provides one. These dates answer different questions.

Read the conditions attached to an old fact. A historical price might be accurately described as historical; presenting it as the current price creates a different claim. Do not remove useful history simply because it is old.

Before relying on an answer for today's product decision, inspect the vendor's current primary page. The five historical stale labels do not establish which facts remain stale today, and this page does not supply a correction workflow for every product change.

before.body:
# Does Google-Extended control AI Overview or AI Mode visibility?

No. Google-Extended covers certain training and grounding uses in other Google systems; its Search AI features use Googlebot and Search preview controls, according to the guide we read on 28 October 2026. Our own 4 August collection recorded 258 Overview results in 280 main searches, but did not test Google-Extended settings. Those counts cannot establish what a bot-policy change would cause.

## What we measured

**Reported.** Google's [AI-feature guide](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/ai-features), read on 28 October 2026, identifies Googlebot robots directives as controls for Search crawling. It lists Search preview controls for limiting information shown from pages, and refers separately to Google-Extended for training and grounding in some other Google systems. Our bot-access reference also records a 20 October review of Google's crawler documentation.

**Measured.** The [Volume III collection](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.21789120) recorded 258 successful Overviews and 22 searches without an Overview among 280 main Google searches on 4 August 2026. These are answer-status observations from a dated question set. The study did not vary website access policies, audit each vendor's robots rules or test an inclusion intervention.

**Reasoned.** A training or grounding policy should be judged for its stated purpose. A Search visibility question requires the Search-specific eligibility and access checks. Neither allowing a documented crawler nor seeing an Overview in a study guarantees that a particular page will be selected as a supporting link.

[Our answer-study method, v1.1.](https://broadcastwell.com/methodology)

## What this means for you

Before changing a crawler rule, identify the purpose you intend to control. Keep that policy decision separate from a claim that your company will appear in an AI answer.

For Search inclusion, inspect the actual page's crawl access, indexing eligibility and snippet eligibility using the relevant Google documentation. A generic statement that “AI bots are allowed” does not tell you which access condition applies.

When reporting an answer observation, save the date and the visible result. If you want to attribute a later difference to an access change, that needs evidence beyond the historical Overview counts given here.

## Also asked as

Does Google-Extended control AI Overview or AI Mode visibility?

## Related

- [Volume III observation record](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.21789120)
- [Bot access and Search eligibility](https://docs.broadcastwell.com/resources/bot-access/)
- [Who gets cited](https://docs.broadcastwell.com/who-gets-cited/)
- [What an AI Overview is](https://docs.broadcastwell.com/answers/google-ai/what-is-a-google-ai-overview/)

## Next step

Use [Free 10-question check (one engine)](https://audit.broadcastwell.com/) to observe an answer after making a separate, informed access-policy decision; the result does not certify the policy. No email is needed; runs are limited per network and per day, and by the site's daily allowance.

If an accessible source contains the factual mistake used in an answer, [Fix one answer, $490](https://broadcastwell.com/answer-repair) can address that source-backed problem. It does not sell crawler permission or guaranteed Search selection.

Prepared by the Broadcastwell team.

# How does Google AI Mode choose cited sources?

Google describes related searches and supporting-page eligibility, but its public guidance does not give a complete formula for which source AI Mode will cite. Our own example is narrower: AI Mode named Procore in 3 of 3 answers to one construction-software question on 22 September 2026. That naming result cannot reveal which sources the system selected or why.

## What we measured

**Reported.** Google's [AI-feature documentation](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/ai-features), read on 28 October 2026, says AI Mode may issue related searches across subtopics and data sources while developing a response. Supporting pages must be indexed and eligible for a Google Search snippet. The guide also says that meeting requirements does not guarantee crawling, indexing or serving.

**Measured.** The [September release](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22907695) captured three scheduled AI Mode answers for the small-residential-builder construction question. All three named Procore, yielding a descriptive 95% Wilson interval of 43.9% to 100.0%. The recorded engine-by-question result is a name count. It is not an engine-specific own-domain citation count or an observation of Google's internal selection process.

**Reasoned.** An answer's visible links can show which destinations were attached to that captured response. They do not expose every page considered, a ranking weight or a causal path from a website edit to a citation. Google's reported mechanisms and our observed answers must retain those separate roles.

[Every figure comes from the published method, v1.1.](https://broadcastwell.com/methodology)

## What this means for you

If you want to understand a citation, begin with the captured answer and its exact links. Read the destination and identify the passage that supports the associated claim. A name appearing elsewhere in the answer is a separate observation.

Check ordinary Search eligibility before seeking an undocumented AI-specific trick. Google's guide says that no special AI text file or schema is required for these features; it does not promise selection after any one technical change.

Keep an honest gap in your report when source-selection evidence is unavailable. A naming table can answer “was this product named?” without answering “why was this page cited?”

# Do YouTube transcripts affect LLM citations?

21 of 148 eligible answers cited a YouTube URL in our [23 October 2026 PHP2Shell study](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23586713), but the data does not establish whether a transcript affected those citations. The collection preserves returned answers and source URLs.

## What we measured

**Measured.** The [PHP2Shell study method and complete answers](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23586713) scheduled ten questions, three returns and five engines. Two Overview targets were excluded, leaving 148 eligible answers. We counted an eligible answer once when its citations contained a YouTube-domain URL, even if it contained several video links.

| Engine | Answers with a recorded YouTube URL | Eligible-answer base |
| --- | --- | --- |
| ChatGPT | 0 | 30 |
| Claude | 0 | 30 |
| Perplexity | 0 | 30 |
| Google AI Overviews | 12 | 28 |
| Google AI Mode | 9 | 30 |

The final grading records classify eighteen of those twenty-one answers Incomplete, two Correct and one Wrong. The capture did not compare edited transcripts.

**Reasoned.** A cited video is an observed source reference. Its presence can be counted alongside the answer's grade.

## What this means for you

Count the returned answers. Two Mode returns to the opening fix question contain the same watch URL, ending BAoKuAB2h_E. They contribute two answer observations, rather than two distinct videos. Other retained sources use YouTube's shorts path; the collection preserves that URL form without supplying a transcript field.

The engine bases matter. The Overview column has twenty-eight eligible answers because two targets were excluded; Mode retains thirty. Pooling their twenty-one citing answers with the other engines gives the 148-answer base above. It would be a different measure to divide by the number of unique video IDs or by all scheduled targets.

# Which tools can track whether my website appears in Google AI Overviews?

The [seoClarity guide](https://www.seoclarity.net/research/ai-overviews-impact) describes AIO query filters, linked-domain details and SERP Previews. Our [September Index](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22907695) shows what a website-level count looks like: HubSpot's own site was a recorded reference in 6 of 30 CRM answer captures from Google AI Overviews on 22 September 2026.

## What we measured

**Measured.** The [Index method and release](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22907695) use ten fixed CRM questions with three Overview returns apiece. All 30 belong to the original valid-answer base. Six contain a HubSpot-domain URL, counted once per answer even when an answer has several links. The same engine named HubSpot CRM in 20 of those 30 answers. This panel does not test seoClarity's accuracy, account access or a change in visitors.

**Reported.** seoClarity's page was last updated on 23 October 2025 and read on 29 October 2026. Its tracking section describes an AI Overviews filter in SERP Features, checks for whether a site or competitor is linked or referenced, and SERP Previews for reading the AIO content. The research discussed on that page uses UK desktop keyword data from September 2024 to September 2025.

**Reasoned.** HubSpot's six website-reference answers and twenty name-containing answers would give different rates from the same 30-return panel. A tool comparison therefore needs to identify which of those units its visibility field represents.

## What this means for you

Use the reference field. In the published seoClarity description, the AIO filter identifies triggering queries, the domain detail addresses the linked site, and SERP Preview shows the answer content. Those are different jobs within a website-appearance check. If your report concerns a page being referenced, a brand-name total alone leaves out the URL that connects the answer to your site.

Keep the referenced page with the count. Our six HubSpot-domain cases contain two distinct product URLs, rather than six different HubSpot pages. Four answer records reference the sales product URL and two reference the CRM product URL. That distinction lets you separate repeated appearances of a page from the number of pages an answer engine referenced. The recorded paths are `/products/sales` and `/products/crm`.

## Also asked as

Which tools can track whether my website appears in Google AI Overviews?

## Related

- [seoClarity's dated AIO tracking description](https://www.seoclarity.net/research/ai-overviews-impact)

# Which tools can track whether my website appears in Google AI Overviews?

The [seoClarity guide](https://www.seoclarity.net/research/ai-overviews-impact) describes AIO query filters, linked-domain details and SERP Previews. Our [September Index](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22907695) shows what a website-level count looks like: HubSpot's own site was a recorded reference in 6 of 30 CRM answer captures from Google AI Overviews on 22 September 2026.

## What we measured

**Measured.** The [Index method and release](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22907695) use ten fixed CRM questions with three Overview returns apiece. All 30 belong to the original valid-answer base. Six contain a HubSpot-domain URL, counted once per answer even when an answer has several links. The same engine named HubSpot CRM in 20 of those 30 answers. This panel does not test seoClarity's accuracy, account access or a change in visitors.

**Reported.** seoClarity's page was last updated on 23 October 2025 and read on 29 October 2026. Its tracking section describes an AI Overviews filter in SERP Features, checks for whether a site or competitor is linked or referenced, and SERP Previews for reading the AIO content. One comparison in the guide covers UK desktop keywords from September 2024 to September 2025; other sections report U.S. desktop and mobile data.

**Reasoned.** HubSpot's six website-reference answers and twenty name-containing answers would give different rates from the same 30-return panel. A tool comparison therefore needs to identify which of those units its visibility field represents.

## What this means for you

Use the reference field. In the published seoClarity description, the AIO filter identifies triggering queries, the domain detail addresses the linked site, and SERP Preview shows the answer content. Those are different jobs within a website-appearance check. If your report concerns a page being referenced, a brand-name total alone leaves out the URL that connects the answer to your site.

Keep the referenced page with the count. Our six HubSpot-domain cases contain two distinct product URLs, rather than six different HubSpot pages. Four answer records reference the sales product URL and two reference the CRM product URL. That distinction lets you separate repeated appearances of a page from the number of pages an answer engine referenced. The recorded paths are `/products/sales` and `/products/crm`.

## Also asked as

Which tools can track whether my website appears in Google AI Overviews?

## Related

- [seoClarity's dated AIO tracking description](https://www.seoclarity.net/research/ai-overviews-impact)
- [The September Index method and data](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22907695)
- [The Manual on valid measurement](https://docs.broadcastwell.com/valid-measurement/)
- [Checking whether a citation supports its claim](https://docs.broadcastwell.com/answers/measurement/how-can-i-check-whether-an-ai-citation-supports-its-claim/)
- [CRM buyer questions](https://index.broadcastwell.com/questions/crm/)

## Next step

Use the [Free 10-question check (one engine)](https://audit.broadcastwell.com/) for a separate dated company-answer sample. No email is needed; runs are limited per network and per day, and by the site's daily allowance.

For one documented company-fact error, [Fix one answer, $490](https://broadcastwell.com/answer-repair). Keep the retained answer and its supporting public source with the correction.

[Every figure comes from the published method, v1.1.](https://broadcastwell.com/methodology)

Prepared by the Broadcastwell team.
